new.title: 7-cycle edges, 10 fan-in-2 AND/OR/NOT gates: some circuit reads x_0 only via an OR at gate 8 with wire 13, true where x_0,x_1,x_6 are false, under a later AND
new.statement: ∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (i k : Fin C.gates.length), i.val = 8 ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size = 10 ∧ (∀ x : Fin 7 → Bool, C.eval (List.ofFn x) = ((x 0 && x 1) || (x 1 && x 2) || (x 2 && x 3) || (x 3 && x 4) || (x 4 && x 5) || (x 5 && x 6) || (x 6 && x 0))) ∧ 0 ∈ (C.gates.get i).inputs ∧ (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length, 0 ∈ (C.gates.get j).inputs → j = i) ∧ (C.gates.get i).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or ∧ (C.gates.get k).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∧ i.val < k.val ∧ 7 + i.val ∈ (C.gates.get k).inputs ∧ 13 ∈ (C.gates.get i).inputs ∧ 13 ≠ 0 ∧ 13 < 7 + i.val ∧ ∃ x : Fin 7 → Bool, x 0 = false ∧ x 1 = false ∧ x 6 = false ∧ (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD 13 false = true
new.unlocks: One of the 90 keys that split whether a least circuit of the 7-cycle can read an input only through one OR under an AND: no two keys fit one circuit, and a no on all 90 is a no for every such circuit.
new.sketch: For the some-circuit side: one explicit list of 10 gates with the OR at gate 8 listing x_0 and wire 13 and an AND after it listing that OR, right on the 128 inputs by decide, and one input for the last clause. For the no-circuit side: gate 8 is an OR listing x_0 and wire 13 and no other gate lists x_0; split on the other gates, or write these gate lists as clauses and replay a solver certificate inside Lean (the checker takes no native_decide). 10 is the least size of this function (a checked row), so no gate is spare. Too large for one file? Hand it back and it is cut again by another gate.

changed.title: Small cases only: on the one-a-side n by n promise, n >= 3, an AND/OR/NOT circuit of s gates gives an AND/OR one of at most s + 2n - 5 gates
changed.statement: ∀ (n s : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit), 3 ≤ n → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C → C.size ≤ s → PEqualNP.Represents.Represents A C → PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost A (s + (2 * n - 5))
changed.unlocks: settles this statement on the record; whichever side is proved is kept
changed.context: Truth unknown; our support is small cases only. A circuit with NOT gates right on the promise is turned into one without, paying at most 2n - 5 more gates. The exclusive-OR graph shows the slope cannot be lower: 4 gates with NOT against exactly 2n - 1 without, a gap of 2n - 5. At side 3 the bound is 1 above; a 3 by 3 graph costing 6 with NOT gates and 8 or more without would break it. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
changed.sketch: Merge duplicate lines. Restriction costs no gates. Restoring a line costs at most one OR. In the reduced r by c table, two unread lines in a bank would match. At least r+c-2 raw wires reach the output, requiring r+c-3 binary gates. At that budget the source is positive. One gate higher, a live NOT forces a tree with one use per wire and one omitted line per bank. On mask 14303 only full lines can be omitted. Derive a terminal NOT by polarity: a six-gate source would give a five-gate complement, below its checked minimum of six. Then tackle larger budgets.

changed.title: Disjoint row probes give a superlinear De Morgan formula lower bound for cyclic window SAT
changed.statement:
∀ d b p q : ℕ,
  let w := d + 1
  let B := b + 1
  let L := 3 * w * 2 ^ d
  let n := L + B * w + p * w + q * (w + 1)
  let hn : 0 < n := by dsimp [n, L, B, w]; positivity
  let stride := 2 ^ (w + 1)
  let I := n * stride
  ∀ F : PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.DMFormula I,
    (∀ table : Fin n → (Fin (w + 1) → Bool) → Bool,
      let x := fun a : Fin I =>
        table ⟨(a.val / stride) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩ (fun j => a.val.testBit j.val)
      F.eval x = true ↔ ∃ word : Fin n → Bool, ∀ i : Fin n,
        table i (fun k => word ⟨(i.val + k.val) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩) = true) →
    B * 4 ^ d ≤ F.leaves
changed.unlocks: bounds literal occurrences of a De Morgan formula deciding cyclic window satisfiability on the full table
changed.context: Vary the matrix prefix to obtain 2^(4^d) different functions of one probe block. A query to a differing matrix entry distinguishes each pair. Let r(F) count nonconstant restrictions to the block and t count its literals. At an AND or OR with children G,H, a nonconstant restriction is one child or a gate on two nonconstant children. Hence 1+r(F)≤(1+r(G))(1+r(H))≤2^t by induction. Adding the two constants gives at most 2^t+1 functions. The block is essential, so t≥1 and t≥4^d. Sum over the disjoint blocks. Allow 60 minutes. A gate-saving companion cannot exist for a count of literal occurrences.

changed.title: Adaptive branching programs need superlinearly many states on cyclic window SAT tables
changed.statement:
∀ d b p q : ℕ,
  let w := d + 1
  let B := b + 1
  let L := 3 * w * 2 ^ d
  let n := L + B * w + p * w + q * (w + 1)
  let hn : 0 < n := by dsimp [n, L, B, w]; positivity
  let stride := 2 ^ (w + 1)
  let I := n * stride
  ∀ P : PEqualNP.BranchingProgram.Program,
    P.Forward → P.ReadsBelow I →
    (∀ table : Fin n → (Fin (w + 1) → Bool) → Bool,
      let x := List.ofFn (fun a : Fin I =>
        table ⟨(a.val / stride) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩ (fun j => a.val.testBit j.val))
      P.eval x = true ↔ ∃ word : Fin n → Bool, ∀ i : Fin n,
        table i (fun k => word ⟨(i.val + k.val) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩) = true) →
    B * 4 ^ d ≤ (4 * d + 2) * P.size
changed.unlocks: counts adaptive query states needed to decide satisfiability from the whole cyclic table
changed.context: Address probes yield 2^(4^d) residual functions on each of B disjoint blocks. If t states read this block, the compression lemma gives at most (t+2)((t+1)!)² functions. The block is essential, so t≥1. If t<4^d then t+1≤4^d and (t+1)!≤(t+1)^t. Also t+2≤2^(2t). The count is at most 2^((4d+2)t), giving 4^d≤(4d+2)t. For t≥4^d the same inequality is immediate. Each state queries one input, so summing over disjoint row blocks charges each state at most once. Allow 60 minutes. A gate-saving companion cannot exist for the size of a branching program.

changed.title: One circuit turns an input function table into deterministic shift-register feedback for all starting states
changed.statement:
∀ d : ℕ,
  let p := d + 1
  let w := p + 1
  let rows := w * (p + 2)^2
  let I := 2^d * d
  let D := Fin d → Bool
  let State := Fin w → Bool
  let active := fun (v : D) => Fin.cons (α := fun _ : Fin w => Bool) false
    (Fin.cons (α := fun _ : Fin p => Bool) false v)
  ∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
    (out : Fin rows → State → Fin (I + C.size)),
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack I C ∧ C.output < I + C.size ∧
    C.size ≤ 128 * 2^p * (p+2)^3 ∧
    ∀ f : D → D,
      let inp := (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin (2^d) => List.ofFn
        (f (fun j => i.val.testBit (d - 1 - j.val))))).flatten
      ∀ v : D, (List.finRange rows).foldl (fun (s : State) row =>
        Fin.snoc (α := fun _ : Fin w => Bool) (fun j : Fin p => s j.succ)
          ((C.wires inp).getD (out row s).val false)) (active v) = active (f v)
changed.unlocks: Supplies shared feedback wires for compiling input-dependent destinations into cyclic tables.
changed.context: Sort data keyed by f(x) with a marker preceding all data of each destination. Save each bitonic swap control and route the starting index through the swaps. At descending power-of-two strides move backward if the lower index exists and has the same key. Three sweeps load the guard, conditionally subtract the stride from high bit to low bit, and clear the guard. This reaches the marker. Reverse the saved swaps and clear its tag. All starts use the same controls.

changed.title: Repeated scans compute cyclic solution parity by retaining one batch of boundary seeds per pass
changed.statement:
∀ (n w p : Nat), 0 < n → 0 < w → 0 < p →
  let D := 2^w
  let slots := (D+p-1)/p
  let Row := Nat → Bool
  let parity := fun (rows : Nat → Row) =>
    ((List.range (2^n)).filter (fun word => (List.range n).all (fun site =>
      let pat := (List.range (w+1)).foldl (fun (acc bit : Nat) =>
        acc ||| ((word.testBit ((site+bit)%n)).toNat <<< bit)) 0
      rows site pat))).length.testBit 0
  let run := fun (S : Nat) (start : Fin S)
      (step : Nat → Nat → Fin S → Row → Fin S) (table : Nat → Row) =>
    (List.range p).foldl (fun prev passId =>
      (List.range n).foldl (fun state siteId => step passId siteId state (table siteId)) prev) start
  let S := 2^(D*slots+1)
  ∃ (start : Fin S) (step : Nat → Nat → Fin S → Row → Fin S) (answer : Fin S → Bool),
    ∀ input : Nat → Row, answer (run S start step input) = parity input
changed.unlocks: bounds the state needed for exact count parity with a prescribed number of passes
changed.context: Partition D seeds into p batches of at most ceil(D/p), allowing empty batches. Initialize the retained endpoint vectors to unit rows. At each table row XOR over allowed incoming transitions. On the last row of a pass XOR the updated diagonal bits into one running bit and initialize the next batch. Summing the disjoint batches returns the trace modulo two, including when the window exceeds the cycle length. The pass and site are supplied to the transition.

changed.title: Cyclic window tables encode the exact size of a Boolean matrix intersection
changed.statement:
∀ (d p q : ℕ),
  let w := d + 1
  let D := Fin d → Bool
  let L := 3 * w * 2 ^ d
  let R := L + p * w + q * (w + 1)
  let n := L + R
  let pos := fun (i : ℕ) => (⟨i % n, Nat.mod_lt _ (Nat.add_pos_left (Nat.mul_pos (Nat.mul_pos (Nat.succ_pos 2) (Nat.succ_pos d)) (Nat.pow_pos (Nat.succ_pos 1))) _)⟩ : Fin n)
  let Part := fun k : ℕ => Fin k → (Fin (w + 1) → Bool) → Bool
  let accepts := fun (P : Part L) (Q : Part R) (word : Fin n → Bool) =>
    (∀ i : Fin L, P i (fun j => word (pos (i.val + j.val))) = true) ∧
    (∀ k : Fin R, Q k (fun t => word (pos (L + k.val + t.val))) = true)
  let projection := fun (k : ℕ) (enc : (D → D → Bool) → Part k) =>
    ∀ row pat, (∃ c : Bool, ∀ M, enc M row pat = c) ∨
      ∃ u v : D, ∀ M, enc M row pat = M u v
  ∃ (first : (D → D → Bool) → Part L) (last : (D → D → Bool) → Part R),
    projection L first ∧ projection R last ∧
    (∀ A B : D → D → Bool,
      (Finset.univ.filter (accepts (first A) (last B))).card =
        (Finset.univ.filter (fun e : D × D => A e.1 e.2 = true ∧ B e.1 e.2 = true)).card) ∧
    ∀ (s : ℕ) (save : Part L → Fin s) (finish : Fin s → Part R → Bool),
      (∀ A B, finish (save (first A)) (last B) = true ↔
        ∃ x, accepts (first A) (last B) x) → 2 ^ (4 ^ d) ≤ s
changed.unlocks: bounds the information retained at a cut when a deterministic procedure reads the table portions in order
changed.context: Use the tagged transfer for A. Transpose B and complement its tag to run in reverse. Pin tag 0 at the start and tag 1 at the cut. Each returning path makes one switch in each half, uniquely for a common entry (u,v), and spells one indexed cyclic word. Pad by w copy steps or w+1 steps appending window parity. The latter gives an even-parity block and then reproduces the original bits. For two different A choose B supported on a single differing entry. Their cut states must differ, so all 2^(4^d) matrices need distinct states. A gate-saving companion cannot exist for a cut-state count.

changed.title: Four independently varying cyclic column modes on the four-by-five permanent level must each be a line (exploration)
changed.statement:
∀ (ζ : ℂ), IsPrimitiveRoot ζ 5 →
  ∀ U : Fin 4 → Submodule ℂ (Fin 4 → ℂ),
    (∀ r, U r ≠ ⊥) →
    (∀ r, ∀ v ∈ U r, (∑ i, v i) = 0) →
    (∀ x : Fin 4 → Fin 4 → ℂ, (∀ r, x r ∈ U r) →
      (∑ f : Fin 4 ↪ Fin 5, ∏ i : Fin 4,
        (1 + ∑ r : Fin 4, x r i * ζ ^ ((r.val+1)*(f i).val))) = 120) →
    ∀ r, Module.finrank ℂ (U r) = 1
changed.unlocks: Excludes a five-dimensional space made from all four independent column modes. Seat-gct-2 reads the return.
changed.context: Relabel a doubled mode as mode 1. Write its centred columns in Hadamard coordinates, with plane U=(a,b,sa+tb). Pick nonzero y,z,w in modes 2,3,4. Extract the pair coefficients u·w=y·z=0, cubic z·q(u)=0 and quartics y·D(u)=w·D(y)=0, where qᵢ=uⱼuₖ and Dᵢ=uᵢ(2uᵢ²−Σuⱼ²). Normalize w=(-s,-t,1). If st is nonzero the cubic forces z=0. Otherwise swap axes so s=0. Coefficient comparison gives tz₁=tz₂+z₃=y₁=y₂+ty₃=0. For t nonzero the dot product gives ty₃z₂=0. At t=0 the last quartic gives y₃³=0. Both cases contradict the choices.

changed.title: Ranking and unranking accepted words of a layered binary automaton by bounded earlier-wire Boolean circuits
changed.statement:
∀ (l q : ℕ), 0 < l → ∀ (start : Fin q) (step : Fin l → Fin q → Bool → Fin q)
  (final : Fin q → Bool),
  let W := Fin l → Bool
  let good := Finset.univ.filter (fun word : W =>
    final ((List.finRange l).foldl (fun s j => step j s (word j)) start) = true)
  let key := fun x : W => ∑ i : Fin l, if x i then 2^(l-1-i.val) else 0
  let rank := fun x : W => (good.filter (fun z => key z < key x)).card
  let valid := fun C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit =>
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack l C ∧
    (∀ g ∈ C.gates, ((g.op = .and ∨ g.op = .or) ∧ g.inputs.length = 2) ∨
      (g.op = .not ∧ g.inputs.length = 1)) ∧ C.size ≤ 256*(l+1)^2*(q+1)^2
  ∃ (select : Fin good.card ≃ ↥good)
    (enc dec : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
    (ew : Fin l → Fin (l+enc.size)) (dw : Fin l → Fin (l+dec.size)),
    valid enc ∧ valid dec ∧ ∀ (r : Fin good.card) (j : Fin l),
      rank (select r).val = r.val ∧
      (enc.wires (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin l => r.val.testBit i.val))).getD (ew j).val false =
        (select r).val j ∧
      (dec.wires (List.ofFn (select r).val)).getD (dw j).val false = r.val.testBit j.val
changed.unlocks: supplies circuit encoders and decoders for enumerated rare Hamming differences
changed.context: Hardwire the number of accepted completions from each layer and state. On an index below the root count, compare it with the zero-child count. Take zero if smaller, otherwise take one and subtract that count. Ranking runs the same path on the word, adding exactly the skipped zero-child counts. These intervals partition each parent's accepted suffixes in lexicographic order. Use l+1 bits for counts, one-hot state wires, and ripple comparisons and updates. Unrolling all layers gives the stated gate bound.

changed.title: Exact rational state dimension of a corrected cyclic syndrome trace at regular parameters
changed.statement:
∀ (r : ℕ) (z : ℚ),
  let A := Fin r → ZMod 2
  let q : ℕ := 2^r
  let f := fun a : A => if a = 0 then z-1 else -1
  let T : A → Matrix (Option A) (Option A) ℚ := fun h before after =>
    before.elim (after.elim 1 (fun b => if b = h then 1 else 0))
      (fun a => after.elim (f a) (fun b => if b = a+h then 1 else 0))
  let cycle := fun w : List A =>
    Matrix.trace (w.map T).prod + f w.sum - (if w.sum = 0 then (q : ℚ) else 0)
  let fits := fun (k : ℕ) (test : List A → Prop) =>
    ∃ (u v : Fin k → ℚ) (M : A → Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℚ),
      ∀ w : List A, test w → (∑ i : Fin k, ∑ j : Fin k, u i * (w.map M).prod i j * v j) = cycle w
  0 < r → z ≠ 0 → z ≠ 2 → z ≠ (q : ℚ) →
    let least : ℕ := (q+1)^2 + (if z = 2*(q : ℚ) then q-1 else q)
    ∀ k : ℕ, (fits k (fun _ => True) ↔ least ≤ k) ∧
      (fits k (fun w => 0 < w.length) ↔ least ≤ k)
changed.unlocks: Prices conversion of an entire corrected cyclic transfer summand into a rational linear scan, including the cost on positive cycle lengths alone.
changed.context: Fourier expansion gives the transfer trace and one scalar correction per character. Invert T0 to recover translations. Fourier projectors isolate each nontrivial character. An excursion through any one of these isolates empty inside the trivial block, giving all matrix units. The word algebra surjects onto the product of the matrix block and surviving characters. Its trace pairing is nondegenerate, giving the Hankel rank. Varying the empty word adds an independent scalar block. Full sketch in barriers/statements/graph-isotropic-code/cyclic-rank.sketch.txt.

changed.title: Exact state dimensions at the singular parameters of the corrected cyclic syndrome trace
changed.statement:
∀ (r : ℕ) (z : ℚ),
  let A := Fin r → ZMod 2
  let q : ℕ := 2^r
  let f := fun a : A => if a = 0 then z-1 else -1
  let T : A → Matrix (Option A) (Option A) ℚ := fun h before after =>
    before.elim (after.elim 1 (fun b => if b = h then 1 else 0))
      (fun a => after.elim (f a) (fun b => if b = a+h then 1 else 0))
  let cycle := fun w : List A =>
    Matrix.trace (w.map T).prod + f w.sum - (if w.sum = 0 then (q : ℚ) else 0)
  let fits := fun (k : ℕ) (test : List A → Prop) =>
    ∃ (u v : Fin k → ℚ) (M : A → Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℚ),
      ∀ w : List A, test w → (∑ i : Fin k, ∑ j : Fin k, u i * (w.map M).prod i j * v j) = cycle w
  (r = 0 ∨ z = 0 ∨ z = 2 ∨ z = (q : ℚ)) →
    let least : ℕ := if r = 0 then (if z = 1 then 1 else if z = 2 then 2 else 3)
      else if z = 0 then 3
      else if z = 2 then (if q = 2 then 2 else q^2+q+1)
      else q^2
    ∀ k : ℕ, (fits k (fun _ => True) ↔ least ≤ k) ∧
      (fits k (fun w => 0 < w.length) ↔ (if z = 2 then least-1 else least) ≤ k)

changed.title: Exceptional trace directions count the exact even-degree defect and give a one-step product extension from every binary subspace
changed.statement:
let F := ZMod 2
∀ (K : Type) [Field K] [Algebra F K] [FiniteDimensional F K] [Fintype K],
  let k := Module.finrank F K
  let dim := fun (L : Submodule F K) => Module.finrank F L
  let sq := fun (L : Submodule F K) =>
    Submodule.span F (Set.range (fun ij : L × L => (ij.1 : K) * (ij.2 : K)))
  let extend := fun (L : Submodule F K) (x : K) => L ⊔ Submodule.span F {x}
  k % 2 = 0 → ∀ L : Submodule F K,
    let W := sq L
    let c := k - dim W
    let e := dim L + 1
    let exceptional := fun a : K => a ≠ 0 ∧ a ∈ L ∧
      ∀ w ∈ W, Algebra.trace F K ((a⁻¹)^2 * w) = 0
    let E := (@Finset.filter K exceptional (fun a => Classical.propDecidable (exceptional a))
      Finset.univ).card
    let loss := if c = e ∧ 0 < E ∧
      2^(dim L) * (2^e - 2) ≤ (E-1) * 2^(k-e) then 1 else 0
    2^e * (∑ x : K, (2^(k - dim (sq (extend L x))) - 1 : ℕ)) =
      2^k * ((2^c - 1) + E) ∧
    ∃ x : K, dim (extend L x) = min k e ∧
      min k (dim W + e) - loss ≤ dim (sq (extend L x))
changed.unlocks: identifies the exceptional directions behind the degree-two discrepancy and bounds the cost of extending an installed product dictionary in every even degree
changed.context: Count pairs (x,b) with nonzero b annihilating the enlarged products. The square test is dependent exactly for b=a^(-2) with a in L. Those E tests admit twice as many x. Bound E by both 2^r-1 and 2^c-1. For c<e the mean is below one. For c>e subtract the baseline and compare to the next jump. At c=e the mean is below three. If all choices miss at least one, x in L alone supply surplus 2^r(2^e-2). Compare with (E-1)2^(k-e). Handle full span directly. Allow 120 to 240 minutes.

changed.title: Mixed row and address gates admit parallel affine pieces with the same row slopes at every address
changed.statement:
∀ (k t : ℕ),
  let F := ZMod 2
  let V := Fin k → F
  let Z := Fin t → Bool
  ∀ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (k+t) C →
    (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2 ∧
      (g.op = .and ∨ g.op = .or ∨ g.op = .mod 2 ∨ (g.op = .not ∧ g.inputs.length = 1))) →
    let s := C.gates.countP (fun g => @decide
      ((g.op = .and ∨ g.op = .or) ∧ g.inputs.length = 2) (Classical.propDecidable _))
    let b := min s k
    let I := Fin (2^b)
    ∃ (U : I → Submodule F V) (a : I → V) (p : I → Z → V) (c : I → Z → F),
      (∀ i, Module.finrank F (U i) = k-b) ∧
      (∀ (z : Z) (x : V), ∃! i : I, x-p i z ∈ U i) ∧
      ∀ (i : I) (z : Z) (u : V), u ∈ U i →
        C.eval (List.ofFn (fun j : Fin k => decide ((p i z + u) j = 1)) ++ List.ofFn z) =
          decide (dotProduct (a i) u + c i z = 1)
changed.unlocks: Exposes the row directions preserved at every address by a full circuit.
changed.context: Track every processed wire as an affine form of the free row displacement. On a leaf its slope is shared across addresses and its offset can vary. At a binary AND or OR split on the value of an operand with nonzero row slope. Both branches survive at every address as parallel cosets of the same kernel. The gate becomes a constant or the other operand on each branch. Affine gates need no split. Refine shallow leaves to codimension b using extra common directions. Equal-sized pieces then number 2^b. A next width beyond the family cannot exist since all widths are included.

changed.title: Removing the last paid gate gives an exact four-term sign identity for a mixed Boolean circuit
changed.statement:
∀ n : ℕ,
  let Circ := PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit
  let legal := fun (nW : ℕ) (C : Circ) =>
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack nW C ∧
      (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2 ∧
        (g.op = .and ∨ g.op = .or ∨ g.op = .mod 2 ∨ (g.op = .not ∧ g.inputs.length = 1)))
  let cost := fun (C : Circ) =>
    C.gates.countP (fun g => @decide
      ((g.op = .and ∨ g.op = .or) ∧ g.inputs.length = 2) (Classical.propDecidable _))
  let sig := fun (v : Bool) => if v then (-1 : ℤ) else 1
  ∀ C : Circ, legal n C → 0 < cost C →
    ∃ D : Fin 4 → Circ,
      (∀ i, legal n (D i) ∧ cost (D i) < cost C) ∧
      ∀ x : Fin n → Bool,
        let bits := List.ofFn x
        2*sig (C.eval bits) = sig ((D 0).eval bits) + sig ((D 1).eval bits) +
          sig ((D 2).eval bits) - sig ((D 3).eval bits)
changed.unlocks: Replaces a paid gate by a pointwise signed sum of cheaper outputs.
changed.context: Cut the last paid gate and propagate affine coefficients through its suffix. If it reaches the output, absorb any linear terms of an OR into the free output form. What remains is AB XOR T, where the prefix supplies A,B,T. The signs of T, T XOR A, T XOR B and T XOR A XOR B have the stated identity by the four possible operand values. If the gate cancels at the output, all four smaller circuits may be identical. A next width beyond this identity cannot exist since it covers every width.

changed.title: Field coefficients on at most two symmetric directions attain the exact service set and arbitrary rank-one directions obey a triangular ceiling
changed.statement:
∀ (E K : Type) [Field E] [CharP E 2] [Fintype E] [Field K] [Algebra E K]
    [FiniteDimensional E K] [Fintype K], 2 < Fintype.card E →
  ∀ (g : ℕ) (ell : K →ₗ[E] E), ell ≠ 0 →
    let m := Module.finrank E K
    let q := Fintype.card E
    let meet := fun (u : Fin g → K) (f : Fin g → (K →ₗ[E] E)) (w : K) (t : ℕ) =>
      w ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ (S : Finset (Fin g)) (a : Fin g → E) (x : K),
        S.card ≤ t ∧ x ≠ 0 ∧ x = w * ∑ i ∈ S, (a i * f i x) • u i
    (∀ (u : Fin g → K) (f : Fin g → (K →ₗ[E] E)) (Z : Finset K),
      (∀ w ∈ Z, meet u f w g) → Z.card + q^(m-g*(g+1)/2) ≤ q^m) ∧
    ∀ d : Fin g → K,
      let P := Submodule.span E (Set.range (fun ij : Fin g × Fin g => d ij.1 * d ij.2))
      let good := meet d (fun i => ell.comp (Algebra.lmul E K (d i)))
      (∀ w : K, (good w g ↔ good w 2) ∧ (good w 2 ↔ ∃ y ∈ P, ell (w*y) ≠ 0)) ∧
        (@Finset.filter K (fun w => good w 2) (fun w => Classical.propDecidable (good w 2))
          Finset.univ).card + q^(m-Module.finrank E P) = q^m
changed.unlocks: bounds the capacity of arbitrary field-coefficient directions and identifies exactly which reciprocals a prescribed symmetric preparation serves

If the diagonal vanishes and H_ij=u is nonzero, put 1/u on i and j to fix the two-cycle. If H is zero, the square of every update vanishes. Count the orthogonal complement. Allow 120 to 240 minutes.

changed.title: The transcript and nonpivot bits of the greedy row scan give a bijection from accepting keys to binomial-tail addresses
changed.statement:
∀ (k r e q : ℕ) (constants : ℕ → Fin (2 ^ k)) (u i : ℕ),
  0 < q → 3 * e + 2 * q + 3 ≤ r → k + e + 3 = 5 * r → u < 2 ^ k → i < k →
  let cut := e + q + 3
  let N := r - e - cut
  let D := e + q - 1
  let m := N - D
  let rot := fun (s wordR : ℕ) =>
    ((wordR <<< (s % k)) ||| (wordR >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun w : ℕ => (List.range k).foldl (fun v b =>
    v ||| ((xor (w.testBit b)
      (!(w.testBit ((b + 1) % k)) && w.testBit ((b + 2) % k))).toNat <<< b)) 0
  let state := fun (key rounds : ℕ) =>
    (List.range rounds).foldl (fun prev t =>
      step (prev ^^^ rot 1 prev ^^^ rot (k - 1) prev) ^^^
        rot (2 * t) key ^^^ (constants (t + 1)).val) (rot 1 key ^^^ u)
  let evenCount := fun tr : List (ℕ × Bool) => (tr.filter (fun item => !item.2)).length
  let scan := fun subject : ℕ =>
    (List.range N).foldl (fun (cfg : Bool × List (ℕ × Bool)) ix =>
      let tr₀ := cfg.2
      let zeros := evenCount tr₀
      let ones := tr₀.length - zeros
      if cfg.1 || decide (m ≤ zeros ∨ D < ones) then cfg
      else
        let t₀ := cut + ix + 1
        let g := D - ones
        if 4 * (r - t₀) < g then (true, tr₀)
        else
          let z := state subject (t₀ - 1)
          let b₀ := (i + 3 * r + k - (3 * t₀ + g)) % k
          let oddGuard := xor (xor (z.testBit b₀) (z.testBit ((b₀ + 1) % k)))
            (z.testBit ((b₀ + 2) % k))
          let pivot := (i + 3 * r + k + 5 - (5 * t₀ + g)) % k
          (false, tr₀ ++ [(pivot, oddGuard)]))
      (false, [])
  let accepted := fun keyA : ℕ =>
    let result := scan keyA
    result.1 = false ∧ evenCount result.2 = m
  let encode := fun keyE : ℕ =>
    let trace := (scan keyE).2
    let pivots := trace.map Prod.fst
    let x := rot 1 keyE ^^^ u
    let rest := ((List.range k).filter (fun freeBit => decide (freeBit ∉ pivots))).map (fun p => x.testBit p)
    ((trace.map Prod.snd) ++ rest).foldr (fun bit acc => bit.toNat + 2 * acc) 0
  Set.BijOn encode {raw : ℕ | raw < 2 ^ k ∧ accepted raw}
    {addr : ℕ | addr < 2 ^ k ∧ ((Finset.range N).filter (fun lowBit => addr.testBit lowBit)).card ≤ D}
changed.unlocks: identifies the exact low-weight addresses for reaching the required number of zero guards
changed.context: Read the low N address bits through zero number m. With f≤D ones and fewer than m zeros, the next trial has 0≤g=D−f≤N−s≤4(r−t). The prefix determines the pivots and 5t+g rises by four or five. Fill the other starting bits in order from the rest of the address. Apply the mixed-target inverse, undo rotation and row XOR. The scan follows those answers and stops at the chosen zero. Encoding returns the address. In the other direction the observed prefix and nonpivots determine the original key. Count addresses by low-word weight. Allow at least 60 minutes.
changed.sketch: Read the low N address bits through zero number m. With f≤D ones and fewer than m zeros, the next trial has 0≤g=D−f≤N−s≤4(r−t). changed.title: One exceptional binomial tail covers every hidden output in a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit for the common-key graph
changed.statement:
∀ (k r e q : Nat), 0 < q → 4 * r + 1 ≤ k → e + q + 4 ≤ r → k + e + 3 = 5 * r →
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit i)
        (!(word.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let constant := fun (j : Nat) => 3 ^ (k + j) % 2 ^ k
  let first := fun (rowKey rowName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun rowState rowIndex =>
      step (rowState ^^^ rot 1 rowState ^^^ rot (k - 1) rowState) ^^^
        rot (2 * rowIndex) rowKey ^^^ constant (rowIndex + 1)) (rot 1 rowKey ^^^ rowName)
  let second := fun (colKey colName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun colState colIndex =>
      step (colState ^^^ rot 2 colState ^^^ rot (k - 2) colState) ^^^
        rot (3 * (colIndex + 1) + 1) colKey ^^^ constant (r + (colIndex + 1)))
      (rot 3 colKey ^^^ colName)
  let h := (k + 1) / 2
  let graph : Fin (2 ^ k) → Fin (2 ^ k) → Bool := fun row col =>
    (List.range (2 ^ k)).any (fun w =>
      decide (first w row.val < 2 ^ (k - h)) && decide (second w col.val < 2 ^ (k - h)))
  let T := min r ((k + 5) / 5)
  let N := T - 4
  let D := e + q - 1
  let exceptions := 2 ^ (k - N) * (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (D + 1), Nat.choose N j)
  D < N →
  ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (k + k) C ∧
    C.size ≤ 256 * (k + 1) * (r + 1) *
      (2 ^ (k - q) + exceptions) ∧
    ∀ bits : Fin (k + k) → Bool,
      C.eval (List.ofFn bits) = PEqualNP.Represents.adjFun (k := k) (l := k) graph bits

changed.context: The ordinary slot zeros the upper copy at H=k+(k-q)-2r+3. Output i=k-q+b-1 has i+3r-H=e+b-1. Use the same N guard bits for every b. If their weight exceeds e+q-1, the cut certificate gives all q pre-key outputs together, so the descending ordinary sweep recovers the passing key. changed.title: Agreement and exact leaf counts for affine partitions predicting a two-round masked parity by cubics
changed.statement:
∀ (k d : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k), (d = 1 ∨ d = 2) → 4 * d + 4 < k →
  let W := Fin k → Bool
  let idx := fun (n : ℕ) => (⟨n % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let add := fun (x y : W) (i : Fin k) => xor (x i) (y i)
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (x : W) (i : Fin k) => x (idx (i.val + k - s % k))
  let mix := fun (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    xor (xor (x i) (x (idx (i.val + d)))) (x (idx (i.val + k - d)))
  let step := fun (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    xor (x i) (!(x (idx (i.val + 1))) && x (idx (i.val + 2)))
  let diff := fun (f : W → Bool) (v x : W) => xor (f x) (f (add x v))
  let stride := 4 * d + 5
  ∀ (s t h : ℕ) (name c₁ c₂ mask : W),
    let observed := fun (key : W) =>
      let initial := mix (add (rot s key) name)
      let middle := add (step initial) (add (rot t key) c₁)
      let out := add (step (mix middle)) (add (rot h key) c₂)
      (List.ofFn (fun bit : Fin k => mask bit && out bit)).foldl xor false
    let weight := (Finset.univ.filter (fun bit : Fin k => mask bit = true)).card
    let packed := ((k / stride) * weight + k - 1) / k
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (leaf : W → Fin n) (query : Fin n → W → W) (answer : Fin n → W)
      (model : Fin n → W → Bool),
      (∀ b x y, query b (add x y) = add (query b x) (query b y)) →
      (∀ b x, leaf x = b ↔ query b x = answer b) →
      (∀ b (v : Fin 4 → W) x, (List.ofFn v).foldl diff (model b) x = false) →
      let signed := Finset.univ.sum (fun sample : W =>
        if observed sample = model (leaf sample) sample then (1 : ℤ) else -1)
      (8 ^ packed * signed.natAbs ^ 4 ≤ 7 ^ packed * (n * 2 ^ k) ^ 4) ∧
      ((∀ x, observed x = model (leaf x) x) → 2 ^ packed ≤ n)
changed.unlocks: bounds cubic agreement and the number of affine cells needed for exact masked parity
changed.context: Average grid shifts to select ≥ p products. On a translate, apply Cauchy-Schwarz twice to sign bias, differencing two designated bits of each product. The remaining pairs have disjoint bilinear terms with independent activation probability 1/4. The cubic leaves an affine phase, so each active pair costs a factor 1/2. Expand each affine cell indicator in parity characters and sum over cells. For exactness each occupied cell has codimension ≥ p by the disjoint-products lemma. A gate-saving companion cannot exist for an affine-cell count.

changed.title: One-sided errors in fan-in-two equality tests preserve the fixed-depth gate exponent on the effective number of names
changed.statement:
let nonlinear := fun (g : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) =>
  (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
  xor (xor (g.op.eval [false, false]) (g.op.eval [false, true]))
      (xor (g.op.eval [true, false]) (g.op.eval [true, true]))
let depth := fun (w : ℕ) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
  (C.gates.foldl (fun (ds : List ℕ) g =>
    ds ++ [(g.inputs.map (fun a => ds.getD a 0)).foldr max 0 + (nonlinear g).toNat])
    (List.replicate w 0)).getD C.output 0
∀ (k a d : ℕ), 0 < k →
  let N := 2^(k+a)
  let b := 2^d
  let groups := min b k
  let value := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (i j : Fin N) =>
    C.eval (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach i j)
  let size := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (i : Fin N) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin N)).filter (fun j => value C i j = true)).card
  let admissible := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
    (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (N+N) C ∧
    depth (N+N) C ≤ d+1 ∧ (∀ i, value C i i = true) ∧
    (∑ i : Fin N, size C i) ≤ N * 2^a
  let price := fun (t B : ℕ) =>
    (∑ u ∈ Finset.range B, Nat.choose (2*t) (u+1)) +
    (∑ v ∈ Finset.range (B-1), Nat.choose (2*t) (v+1))
  (∀ C, admissible C → 2^k ≤ 2 + price (C.gates.countP nonlinear) b) ∧
  ∃ C, admissible C ∧ (∀ i, size C i = 2^a) ∧
    C.gates.countP nonlinear + 1 ≤ (groups + k % groups) * 2^(k / groups - 1)
changed.unlocks: bounds the depth-dependent nonlinear cost when all equal pairs must pass and only the average number of false positives is limited
changed.context: Write N=2^(k+a). By Cauchy-Schwarz the sum of reciprocal row sizes is at least N^2 divided by the total number of ones, hence at least 2^k. The pivot bound gives this much full rank. Removing two anchor functions loses at most two, so apply the depth binomial bound. For the circuit keep k name bits and compare them by the balanced-block construction. changed.title: Perfect matching on a 3 by 3 graph: some normal-form circuit of at most 11 gates opens with AND of wires 0 and 1, then AND of wires 0 and 3
changed.statement:
∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 11 ∧
    (∀ x : Fin 9 → Bool, C.eval (List.ofFn x) = ((x 0 && x 4 && x 8) || (x 0 && x 5 && x 7) || (x 1 && x 3 && x 8) || (x 1 && x 5 && x 6) || (x 2 && x 3 && x 7) || (x 2 && x 4 && x 6))) ∧
    C.output + 1 = 9 + C.size ∧
    (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length,
      ((C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not ∧
          ∃ a, a < 9 + j.val ∧ (C.gates.get j).inputs = [a]) ∨
      (((C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∨
          (C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or) ∧
          ∃ a b, a < b ∧ b < 9 + j.val ∧ (C.gates.get j).inputs = [a, b])) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length,
      (∃ x y : Fin 9 → Bool,
        (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (9 + j.val) false ≠ (C.wires (List.ofFn y)).getD (9 + j.val) false) ∧
      ∀ k, k < 9 + j.val → ∃ x : Fin 9 → Bool,
        (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (9 + j.val) false ≠ (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD k false) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length, j.val + 1 < C.gates.length →
      ∃ k : Fin C.gates.length, j.val < k.val ∧ 9 + j.val ∈ (C.gates.get k).inputs) ∧
    C.gates.head? = some ⟨PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and, [0, 1]⟩ ∧
    C.gates.tail.head? = some ⟨PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and, [0, 3]⟩
changed.unlocks: One case of the cut of 3 by 3 perfect matching at 11 gates by its two earliest gates: with the other cases under the same earliest gate and their cover, the floor for that earliest gate, one of five the assembly takes.
changed.sketch: The two earliest gates are written out and the circuit is in normal form: output last, operands increasing, no constant or repeated wire, every gate but the last listed later. changed.title: Exact cost of repeated rows from neighborhood inclusion in a monotone one-hot table
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : Nat) (A : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (u : Fin n),
  (∃ i j, A i j = false) →
  ∀ (t s : Nat),
    let expanded := fun (i : Fin (n + t)) (j : Fin m) =>
      if h : i.val < n then A ⟨i.val, h⟩ j else A u j
    let extra := if ∃ (j : Fin m) (i : Fin n), A u j = true ∧ A i j = false
      then t else 0
    PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost expanded s ↔
      ∃ b : Nat, PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost A b ∧ b + extra ≤ s
changed.unlocks: Removing all repeated row and column profiles with an exact additive adjustment to the optimum.
changed.context: If u accepts j rejected by i, the empty row bank rejects j, so each twin reaches a gate. Delete a twin and fold the first gate that reads it. Iterate. OR gives the upper. Otherwise all columns accepted by u are full. With none, substitute false for u. With one, substitute its raw column for u. With several, contract them to one. Restoring them costs one each by the strict column case using the surviving zero, before and after copying u. Cancel the equal costs.

changed.title: Small bias of distinct query masks bounds the gain of one XOR-AND circuit bit at every product budget
changed.statement:
∀ (k m h D E : ℕ), 0 < D →
  let F := ZMod 2
  let V := Fin k → F
  ∀ v : Fin m ↪ V, (∀ j, v j ≠ 0) →
    (∀ x : V, x ≠ 0 →
      let n := ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m)).filter (fun j => dotProduct (v j) x = 1)).card
      D*((m : ℤ)-2*(n : ℤ)).natAbs ≤ E*m) →
    ∀ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
      PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack k C →
      (∀ g ∈ C.gates, (g.op = .and ∧ g.inputs.length = 2) ∨
        (g.op = .mod 2 ∧ g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∨
        (g.op = .not ∧ g.inputs.length = 1)) →
      let s := C.gates.countP (fun g => @decide (g.op = .and) (Classical.propDecidable _))
      2*s+h ≤ k → ∀ (K : Finset (Fin m)) (dec : Bool → Fin m → F),
        let bit := fun x : V => C.eval (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin k => decide (x i = 1)))
        let G := 2*(∑ x : V, (K.filter (fun j => dec (bit x) j = dotProduct (v j) x)).card) -
          2^k*K.card
        2^h*D*G^2 ≤ (D+(2^h-1)*E)*m*(2^k)^2
changed.unlocks: Converts a product budget into a bias-dependent bound for any one-bit row predictor.
changed.context: Use nonlinear input compression to put the shared bit in the form of a linear character times a function of 2s parity probes. Its Fourier support lies in their translated span. The one-bit gain squared is at most the captured query count times the squared row count. Enclose that translate in a codimension-h affine flat. Fourier filtering bounds the count in that flat by m(1+(2^h−1)E/D)/2^h. Keeping fewer addresses can only decrease the count on the right. A fixed gate-price bar cannot exist in this bound since s is a parameter.

changed.title: At or below n+m-2 gates a table with only full universally comparable lines is positive or the complement of a smaller positive table circuit
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : Nat) (A : Fin n → Fin m → Bool),
  2 ≤ n → 2 ≤ m →
  Function.Injective A → Function.Injective (fun j i => A i j) →
  (∀ r : Fin n, (∀ i : Fin n, (∀ j, A r j ≤ A i j) ∨ (∀ j, A i j ≤ A r j)) →
    ∀ j, A r j = true) →
  (∀ c : Fin m, (∀ j : Fin m, (∀ i, A i c ≤ A i j) ∨ (∀ i, A i j ≤ A i c)) →
    ∀ i, A i c = true) →
  ∀ s : Nat, s + 2 ≤ n + m →
    ((∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
      C.size ≤ s ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents A C) ↔
    PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost A s ∨
      ∃ b : Nat, b + 1 ≤ s ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun i j => !(A i j)) b)
changed.unlocks: Exclude a six-gate solution from positive minima of the table and its complement at the first budget allowing one useful inversion.
changed.context: Distinct profiles force at least n+m-2 raw leaves. With a useful NOT and the budget, connected edge counting forces a read-once tree with one unary NOT. Exactly one line per bank is omitted. Every other line compares with its omitted line by unateness. The omitted lines are full, so activating any used input decreases some answer. Every leaf lies below the NOT and the NOT is at the root. Remove it to get a positive complement circuit. Append one for the reverse.

changed.title: An eight-site test for a constant difference between two key responses at a fixed-mask two-round column bit
changed.statement:
∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k), 7 ≤ k → k % 3 ≠ 0 →
  let W := Fin k → ZMod 2
  let ix := fun n : ℕ => (⟨n % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (x : W) (i : Fin k) => x (ix (i.val+k-(s % k)))
  let mix := fun (x : W) (i : Fin k) => x i + x (ix (i.val+2)) + rot 2 x i
  let upd := fun (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    let y := mix x
    y i + (1+y (ix (i.val+1)))*y (ix (i.val+2))
  let run := fun (key name c1 c2 : W) =>
    upd (upd (rot 3 key + name) + rot 4 key + c1) + rot 7 key + c2
  ∀ (c1 c2 left right : W) (site : Fin k) (bit : ZMod 2),
    let d := left+right
    Iff (∀ name : W, run left name c1 c2 site + run right name c1 c2 site = bit)
      ((∀ a : Fin 8, mix (rot 3 d) (ix (site.val+k-1+a.val)) = 0) ∧ bit = rot 1 d site)
changed.unlocks: Identifies exactly which raw key differences disappear up to an output offset at each two-round column site with fixed round masks.
changed.context: Use the mixed starting word as the free name coordinate. At site zero the quartic monomials have supports 0134, 0156, 2356, 1245. No two share a triple, so their cubic differences force mixed key differences zero at 0 through 6. The remaining quadratic coefficient forces site −1 zero as well. All name dependence then cancels. The surviving constant is the mixed difference at −2 plus raw d at −7, equal to d at −1 by the zero mixed equation at 0. Rotate this calculation to any site.

changed.title: Exact worst static degree of rejecting cyclic binary pair tables at lengths at least two
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n), 2 ≤ n →
  let P := MvPolynomial (Fin n) (ZMod 2)
  let static := fun (axioms : Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n))) (budget : ℕ) =>
    ∃ (q : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n) → P) (b : Fin n → P),
      (∀ C ∈ axioms, q C = 0 ∨ (q C).totalDegree + (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.clausePoly C).totalDegree ≤ budget) ∧
      (∀ v, b v = 0 ∨ (b v).totalDegree + 2 ≤ budget) ∧
      axioms.sum (fun C => q C * PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.clausePoly C) +
        (∑ v, b v * (MvPolynomial.X v * MvPolynomial.X v + MvPolynomial.X v)) = 1
  let pos := fun i : ℕ => (⟨i % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩ : Fin n)
  let blockers := fun T : Fin n → Bool → Bool → Bool =>
    let blocks := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n × (Bool × Bool))).filter
      (fun z => T z.1 z.2.1 z.2.2 = false)
    blocks.image (fun row =>
      ({(row.1, !row.2.1), (pos (row.1.val+1), !row.2.2)} : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)))
  let rejects := fun candidate : Fin n → Bool → Bool → Bool =>
    ¬ ∃ x : Fin n → Bool, ∀ i : Fin n, candidate i (x i) (x (pos (i.val+1))) = true
  (∀ table, rejects table →
    let G := PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.cnfSystem (↑(blockers table) : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)))
    PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.PCRefutable G 2 ∧ ¬ PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.PCRefutable G 1) ∧
  (∀ d : ℕ, (∀ table, rejects table → static (blockers table) d) ↔ (n = 2 ∧ 2 ≤ d) ∨ n+2 < 2^d)
changed.unlocks: determines the extremal static degree and the dynamic degree for every rejecting pair table
changed.context: Relax the table to a maximal rejecting one. Sum the two blockers per row of an odd twist to get linear equations summing to one. A singleton row normalizes to the anchored cycle. A restricted interval of length ℓ has threshold ℓ+1<2^d. For dynamic calculus, add blockers to derive endpoint units, then propagate in degree two. All input axioms have degree two. At n=2 the four word indicators suffice. The anchored cycle attains the static lower bound. Allow 60 minutes. A gate-saving companion cannot exist for a maximal static proof degree.

changed.title: Exact tag length for a raw prefix and an affine suffix map chosen by that prefix
changed.statement:
∀ k c : ℕ, 0 < k →
  let F := ZMod 2
  let X := Fin k → F
  let Z := Fin (k-1) → F
  let W := X × Z
  let ok := fun (send : W → X) (tag : W → Fin c → Bool) =>

changed.title: The scheduled five-word relation has a linear-size bidirectional ternary encoding and logarithmic reverse propagation is necessary in one round
changed.statement:
∀ (k r : ℕ), (k % 6 = 1 ∨ k % 6 = 5) →
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit i)
        (!(word.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let constant := fun (j : Nat) => 3 ^ (k + j) % 2 ^ k
  let first := fun (rowKey rowName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun rowState rowIndex =>
      step (rowState ^^^ rot 1 rowState ^^^ rot (k - 1) rowState) ^^^
        rot (2 * rowIndex) rowKey ^^^ constant (rowIndex + 1)) (rot 1 rowKey ^^^ rowName)
  let second := fun (colKey colName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun colState colIndex =>
      step (colState ^^^ rot 2 colState ^^^ rot (k - 2) colState) ^^^
        rot (3 * (colIndex + 1) + 1) colKey ^^^ constant (r + (colIndex + 1)))
      (rot 3 colKey ^^^ colName)
  let V := Fin 5 × Fin k
  let word := fun (v : V → Bool) (track : Fin 5) =>
    ∑ j : Fin k, (v (track,j)).toNat * 2^j.val
  let agrees := fun (v : V → Bool) =>
    word v 3 = first (word v 2) (word v 0) ∧
    word v 4 = second (word v 2) (word v 1)
  let project := fun (m : ℕ) (F : Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Sum V (Fin m)))) =>
    (∀ C ∈ F, C.card ≤ 3) ∧ ∀ v : V → Bool, agrees v ↔
      ∃ aux : Fin m → Bool, PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfies (Sum.elim v aux) (↑F : Set _)
  let drive := fun (m : ℕ) (F : Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Sum V (Fin m))))
      (d : ℕ) (rowRev colRev allWires : Bool) => ∀ pins : V → Bool,
    let selected := fun j : V => j.1 = 2 ∨ j.1 = (if rowRev then 3 else 0) ∨
      j.1 = (if colRev then 4 else 1)
    let seed : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Literal (Sum V (Fin m))) :=
      {l | ∃ j : V, selected j ∧ l = (Sum.inl j, pins j)}
    let advance := fun S : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Literal (Sum V (Fin m))) =>
      S ∪ {l | ∃ C ∈ F, l ∈ C ∧ ∀ other ∈ C, other ≠ l →
        PEqualNP.Search.negLit other ∈ S}
    let known := (advance^[d]) seed
    ∃ u : Sum V (Fin m) → Bool,
      PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfies u (↑F : Set _) ∧
      (∀ j : V, selected j → u (Sum.inl j) = pins j) ∧
      ∀ z : Sum V (Fin m), (allWires = true ∨ ∃ j : V, z = Sum.inl j) → (z,u z) ∈ known
  (∃ m F, project m F ∧ m + (∑ C ∈ F, C.card) ≤ 4096*(k+1)*(r+1) ∧
    drive m F (16*(r+1)) false false false ∧
    ∀ revA revB : Bool,
      drive m F (64*(r+1)*(Nat.clog 2 k+1)) revA revB true) ∧
  (r = 1 → ∀ m F d, project m F → drive m F d true false false →
    k + (if k % 6 = 5 then 2 else 0) ≤ 2^d)

changed.title: Crossing pairs and completed mismatch counts bound rectangle covers of a conjunction of central Hamming tests
changed.statement:
∃ N : ℕ, ∀ (n r : ℕ), N ≤ n → 0 < r → 8192*r < n →
  ∀ M : Fin r → Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
    (∀ j l : Fin r, j ≠ l →
      128*(Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin n => M j i = M l i)).card ≤ n) →
    let V := Bool × Fin n
    let X := V → Bool
    ∀ S : Finset V,
      let crosses := fun j : Fin r => (Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin n =>
        ¬ ((false,i) ∈ S ↔ (true,M j i) ∈ S))).card
      let m := Finset.univ.sup crosses
      let accept := fun (x z : X) =>
        let w := fun v : V => if v ∈ S then x v else z v
        ∀ j : Fin r,
          let D := (Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin n => w (false,i) ≠ w (true,M j i))).card
          16 * Nat.dist (2*D) n ≤ n
      let cover := fun u : ℕ => ∃ left right : Fin u → X → Prop,
        ∀ x z : X, accept x z ↔ ∃ t : Fin u, left t x ∧ right t z
      cover ((n+1)^r * 2^(r*m)) ∧
      ∀ u : ℕ, cover u →
        2^(min m (n/128)) ≤ u ∧
        (n ≤ 2*S.card → 2*S.card ≤ 3*n → n/512+1 ≤ u)

changed.title: An exact joint height and branching-rank recurrence on implication paths with unequal private parity blocks
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (w : Fin n → ℕ), (∀ i, 0 < w i) →
  let Raw := (i : Fin n) × Fin (w i)
  let parity := fun (y : Raw → Bool) (i : Fin n) =>
    decide (Odd ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (w i))).filter (fun j => y ⟨i,j⟩ = true)).card)
  let liftAx := fun (F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)))
      (A : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause Raw) =>
    ∃ C ∈ F, ∃ y : Raw → Bool, (∀ lit ∈ C, parity y lit.1 ≠ lit.2) ∧
      A = ((Finset.univ : Finset Raw).filter (fun b => b.1 ∈ C.image Prod.fst)).image
        (fun b => (b, !(y b)))
  let shape := fun (N J : Finset (List Bool)) =>
    [] ∈ N ∧ J ⊆ N ∧
    (∀ (p : List Bool) (b : Bool), p ++ [b] ∈ N → p ∈ J) ∧
    ∀ p ∈ J, p ++ [false] ∈ N ∧ p ++ [true] ∈ N
  let join := fun a b : ℕ => if a = b then a+1 else max a b
  let refutes := fun (F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n))) (H s : ℕ) =>
    ∃ (N J : Finset (List Bool)) (line : List Bool → PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause Raw)
      (r : List Bool → ℕ), shape N J ∧ line [] = ∅ ∧ r [] ≤ s ∧ (∀ p ∈ N, p.length ≤ H) ∧
      (∀ p ∈ N \ J, liftAx F (line p) ∧ r p = 0) ∧
      ∀ p ∈ J, PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsResolvent (line (p ++ [false]))
        (line (p ++ [true])) (line p) ∧ r p = join (r (p ++ [false])) (r (p ++ [true]))
  let F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)) := {C | ∃ e : Fin (n+1),
    C = (((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).filter (fun v => v.val+1 = e.val)).image
      (fun v => (v,false))) ∪ (((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).filter (fun v => v.val = e.val)).image
      (fun v => (v,true)))}
  let feasible : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Prop := Nat.rec
    (fun i j _ _ => i = j)
    (fun _ prev i j H s => i = j ∨ ∃ v : Fin n, i ≤ v.val ∧ v.val < j ∧ w v ≤ H ∧
      ∃ a b : ℕ, (w v-1) + join a b ≤ s ∧ prev i v.val (H-w v) a ∧ prev (v.val+1) j (H-w v) b)
  ∀ H s : ℕ, refutes F H s ↔ feasible n 0 n H s

changed.title: The cost of arbitrarily many identical row copies is determined by a single empty-row response
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : Nat) (A : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (u : Fin n),
  (∃ i j, A i j = false) →
  ∀ (t s : Nat),

      if h : i.val < n then A ⟨i.val, h⟩ j else A u j
    let silent := ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
      PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ C.size ≤ s ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents A C ∧
      ∀ j : Fin m,
        C.eval (List.replicate n false ++ List.ofFn (fun v : Fin m => decide (v = j))) = A u j
    PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost expanded s ↔
      (∃ b : Nat, b + t ≤ s ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost A b) ∨ silent

changed.title: Parity questions for two-round output masks and their fourth differences
changed.statement:
∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k),
  let F := ZMod 2
  let W := Fin k → F
  let D := W →ₗ[F] F
  let ix := fun n : ℕ => (⟨n % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (x : W) (i : Fin k) => x (ix (i.val + k - s % k))
  let mix := fun (g : ℕ) (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    x i + x (ix (i.val + g)) + x (ix (i.val + k - g % k))
  let step := fun (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    x i + (1 + x (ix (i.val + 1))) * x (ix (i.val + 2))
  let gap := fun b : Bool => if b then 2 else (1 : ℕ)
  let spin := fun b : Bool => if b then 3 else (1 : ℕ)
  let diff := fun (f : W → F) (u x : W) => f (x + u) - f x
  let fourth := fun (f : W → F) (v : Fin 4 → W) => (List.ofFn v).foldl diff f
  let cubic := fun (f : W → F) => ∀ v x, fourth f v x = 0
  ∀ (name c₁ c₂ : Bool → W) (d : ℕ),
    let out := fun (x : W) (b : Bool) =>
      let z := mix (gap b) (rot (spin b) x + name b)
      let y := step z + rot (if b then 4 else 0) x + c₁ b
      step (mix (gap b) y) + rot (if b then 7 else 2) x + c₂ b
    let run := fun (ask : Fin d → ℕ → D) (x : W) =>
      (List.finRange d).foldl (fun h j =>
        2 * h + (if ask j h x = 0 then 0 else 1)) (0 : ℕ)
    let top := fun (x : W) (b : Bool) (i : Fin k) =>
      let g := gap b
      let z := mix g (rot (spin b) x)
      let two := fun p : ℕ => z (ix (p + 1)) * z (ix (p + 2))
      let q := fun j : Fin k =>
        two j.val + two (ix (j.val + g)).val + two (ix (j.val + k - g % k)).val
      q (ix (i.val + 1)) * q (ix (i.val + 2))
    ∀ (m : ℕ) (mask : Fin m → Bool → Fin k → F),
      let observe := fun (w : Bool → W) (j : Fin m) =>
        (∑ i, mask j false i * w false i) + (∑ i, mask j true i * w true i)
      (∃ (ask : Fin d → ℕ → D) (readout : ℕ → Fin m → W → F),
        (∀ h j, cubic (readout h j)) ∧
        ∀ x j, observe (out x) j = readout (run ask x) j x) ↔
      (∃ queries : Fin d → D, ∀ (j : Fin m) (v : Fin 4 → W),
        (∀ e n, queries n (v e) = 0) →
        fourth (fun x => observe (top x) j) v (0 : W) = 0)

changed.context: Expand the two updates modulo functions of degree at most three. Only the product of the two neighboring mixed quadratic parts survives, giving top. Fourth differences are independent of the base. Along the zero transcript the queries define a kernel on which all these differences vanish. Conversely, ask the fixed forms. On each fiber pull the target back along an affine retraction onto that fiber. Its fourth differences use only kernel directions and vanish, so this is a global cubic readout.

changed.title: Disjoint two-round windows cost one query per row bit and two per column bit for cubic readout
changed.statement:
let fits := fun (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) (mark : Fin k → Bool × Bool) (d : ℕ)
    (name c₁ c₂ : Bool → Fin k → ZMod 2) =>
  let F := ZMod 2
  let W := Fin k → F
  let D := W →ₗ[F] F
  let ix := fun n : ℕ => (⟨n % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (x : W) (i : Fin k) => x (ix (i.val + k - s % k))
  let mix := fun (g : ℕ) (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    x i + x (ix (i.val + g)) + x (ix (i.val + k - g % k))
  let step := fun (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    x i + (1 + x (ix (i.val + 1))) * x (ix (i.val + 2))
  let gap := fun b : Bool => if b then 2 else (1 : ℕ)
  let spin := fun b : Bool => if b then 3 else (1 : ℕ)
  let diff := fun (f : W → F) (u x : W) => f (x + u) - f x
  let fourth := fun (f : W → F) (v : Fin 4 → W) => (List.ofFn v).foldl diff f
  let cubic := fun (f : W → F) => ∀ v x, fourth f v x = 0
  let out := fun (x : W) (b : Bool) =>
    let z := mix (gap b) (rot (spin b) x + name b)
    let y := step z + rot (if b then 4 else 0) x + c₁ b
    step (mix (gap b) y) + rot (if b then 7 else 2) x + c₂ b
  let run := fun (ask : Fin d → ℕ → D) (x : W) =>
    (List.finRange d).foldl (fun h j =>
      2 * h + (if ask j h x = 0 then 0 else 1)) (0 : ℕ)
  ∃ (ask : Fin d → ℕ → D) (readout : ℕ → Bool → Fin k → W → F),
    (∀ h b i, cubic (readout h b i)) ∧
    ∀ x b i, (if b then (mark i).2 else (mark i).1) = true →
      out x b i = readout (run ask x) b i x
∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k), 7 ≤ k →
  ∀ (mark : Fin k → Bool × Bool) (d : ℕ) (name c₁ c₂ : Bool → Fin k → ZMod 2),
  let ix := fun n : ℕ => (⟨n % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)

    (Finset.range (if b then 11 else 7)).image (fun r =>
      ix (i.val + k - (if b then 5 else 1) % k + r))
  (∀ (b c : Bool) (i j : Fin k), on b i = true → on c j = true →

    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin k)).filter (fun i => (mark i).1 = true)).card +
      2 * ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin k)).filter (fun i => (mark i).2 = true)).card ≤ d)

changed.title: Exact gate cost for a looped star and a disjoint edge when specified leaves must affect the full input cube
changed.statement:
∀ (h t : ℕ), 0 < t →
  let n := 3+h+t

    leaves.filter (fun j => ∃ x : Fin n → Bool,
      C.eval (List.ofFn (Function.update x j false)) ≠ C.eval (List.ofFn (Function.update x j true)))
  (∀ C, visible C → h + 5 + (active C).card ≤ C.size) ∧
    ∀ S : Finset (Fin n), S ⊆ leaves →
      ∃ C, visible C ∧ active C = S ∧ C.size = h+5+S.card

changed.title: Signed counts on joint cyclic difference fibers from paths and cycles of free components
changed.unlocks: Evaluates squared local factors of a schedule spectrum by counting path and cycle components.
changed.context: Parameterize the fiber by independent flips of free components. Each is a cyclic interval. Contracting intervals, deleting pinned sites and cancelling repeated edges leaves paths and cycles. The polar matrix of the restricted phase is their adjacency matrix. On a path a null vector alternates with a forced endpoint neighbor zero. On a cycle it repeats with period two. Odd components contribute one null bit and even cycles two. Apply the binary quadratic radical formula on the flip coordinates. Estimate 140 minutes.

changed.title: A single fork with one branch through the only NOT splits into three positive read-once gate lists that preserve independent cuts
changed.statement:
∀ (N : Nat) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (f t : Fin C.size),
  let atGate := PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C
  let reads := fun (D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) => PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.readsIn D (Finset.range D.size)
  let use := fun (D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (w : Nat) => reads D w + (if D.output = w then 1 else 0)
  let tree := fun (n : Nat) (D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
    (∀ g ∈ D.gates, (g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∨ g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or) ∧ g.inputs.length = 2) ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack n D ∧ (D.output+1 = n+D.size ∨ (D.size = 0 ∧ D.output < n)) ∧
    (∀ i < n, use D i ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ j < D.size, use D (n+j) = 1)
  f < t → C.output+1 = N+C.size → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack N C →
  (∀ g ∈ C.gates, ((g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∨ g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or) ∧ g.inputs.length = 2) ∨
    (g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not ∧ g.inputs.length = 1)) →
  (∀ j : Fin C.size, (atGate j.val).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not ↔ j = t) →
  (∀ i < N, reads C i ≤ 1) →
  (∀ j : Fin C.size, reads C (N+j.val) = if j = f then 2 else if j.val+1 = C.size then 0 else 1) →
  PEqualNP.EdgeOwnership.InCone N C f.val t.val →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.readsIn C (insert t.val (((PEqualNP.EdgeOwnership.cones N C).getD t.val []).toFinset)) (N+f.val) = 1 →
  ∃ W H D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, tree N W ∧ tree (N+1) H ∧ tree (N+2) D ∧
    W.size+H.size+D.size+1 = C.size ∧
    (∀ i < N, use W i + use H i + use D i = reads C i) ∧
    use H N = 1 ∧ use D N = 1 ∧ use D (N+1) = 1 ∧
    ∀ (x : Fin N → Bool) (a b : Bool),
      let xs := List.ofFn x
      let v := C.gates.foldl (fun (ys : List Bool) g =>
        let j := ys.length-N
        ys ++ [if j = f.val then a else if j = t.val then b
               else g.op.eval (g.inputs.map (fun i => ys.getD i false))]) xs
      W.eval xs = (C.wires xs).getD (N+f.val) false ∧
      H.eval (xs++[a]) = v.getD ((atGate t.val).inputs.headD (N+C.size)) false ∧
      D.eval (xs++[a,b]) = v.getD C.output false
changed.unlocks: Exposes the physical read-once regions for pinning in the classification of tight one-hot NOT circuits.
changed.context: Separate the inclusive fork cone, the strict NOT cone outside the fork cone, and every remaining gate except the NOT. No proper predecessor can leave its cone by another use. One fork use goes into the NOT cone and the other goes outside. Cut the NOT output at its unique use. Copy each gate subsequence in order, adding the designated independent input ports. A bare port may be the whole middle tree. Each other raw or internal use belongs to one piece. Apply the trace-copy lemma to independently forced values and add the three disjoint gate counts.

changed.title: A single fair-bit tree minimizes every stopping tail for an integer histogram with prescribed real means
changed.statement:
∀ (q E : ℕ), 0 < q → 0 < E → ∀ μ : Fin q → ℝ, (∀ j, 0 ≤ μ j) → (∑ j, μ j) = E →
  let A := Fin q → ℕ
  let Tree := ℕ → ℕ → Option A
  let pending := fun (T : Tree) (b : ℕ) =>
    ((Finset.range (2^b)).filter (fun i => (T b i).isNone)).card
  let valid := fun T : Tree =>
    (∀ b i v, i < 2^b → T b i = some v →
      (∑ j : Fin q, v j) = E ∧ T (b+1) (2*i) = some v ∧ T (b+1) (2*i+1) = some v) ∧
    Filter.Tendsto (fun b => (pending T b : ℝ)/(2 : ℝ)^b) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) ∧
    ∀ j : Fin q, Filter.Tendsto
      (fun b => ((∑ i ∈ Finset.range (2^b), ((T b i).getD 0) j : ℕ) : ℝ)/(2 : ℝ)^b)
      Filter.atTop (nhds (μ j))
  let bound := fun b : ℕ => 2^b-(∑ j : Fin q, ⌊(2 : ℝ)^b*μ j⌋₊)/E
  (∀ T : Tree, valid T → ∀ b : ℕ, bound b ≤ pending T b) ∧
  (∃ T : Tree, valid T ∧ ∀ b : ℕ, pending T b = bound b) ∧
  Summable (fun b : ℕ => (bound b : ℝ)/(2 : ℝ)^b)
changed.unlocks: Computes the least possible fair-bit stopping tails when a random integer allocation is constrained only through its mean.
changed.context: Stopped prefixes have used at most floor(2^b μ_j) units in coordinate j, since their normalized contribution can only increase. Each spends E units. To grow the tree, copy stopped labels to both children. Fill each residual coordinate capacity with tokens, pack as many E-token groups as possible, and assign one group to each available prefix until the groups run out. The total capacity is at most 2^b E. Fewer than E tokens remain after packing. Coordinate deficits are bounded independently of depth, so normalized means converge. The pending count is bounded and its tail sum converges.

changed.title: A residue criterion decides when one periodic fair-bit path can equalize integer batch counts
changed.statement:
∀ (q E p : ℕ), 1 < q → 0 < E → E < q → 0 < p → 2^p % q = 1 →
  ((∃ v : Fin p → Fin q → ℕ,
    (∀ i, (∑ j, v i j) = E) ∧
    ∀ j, q*(∑ i : Fin p, 2^i.val * v i j) = (2^p-1)*E) ↔
   ∀ b < p, (2^b*E) % q ≤ E)
changed.unlocks: Constructs periodic integer output labels for a finite fair-bit matching predictor with one continuing transition per state.
changed.context: Give each bin capacity M=(2^p-1)E/q. Pack E copies of each power of two from largest to smallest. At size 2^k the exact feasibility test is q floor(M/2^k)≥E(2^(p-k)-1), since larger pieces consumed whole slots. All cuts suffice by greedy placement, and equal total mass fills every bin. Write 2^(p-k)E=qA+r. Then 2^k r is positive and congruent to E modulo q, so it is at least E. Hence floor(M/2^k)=A and the cut says r≤E. The endpoint residues coincide.

changed.title: Above half the shift support a random choice of small circuits has strictly larger worst-case selector error than an unrestricted table
changed.statement:
∀ k a : ℕ, (6 ≤ a ∧ 2*2^a ≤ k) →
  let N := 2^k
  let r := 2^a
  let I := Fin N
  let target := fun (D : Finset ℕ) (x y : I) =>
    xor (x.val.testBit (y.val % r)) (decide (Nat.xor x.val y.val ∈ D))
  let Q := 2^(k/2)
  let fits := fun C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit =>
    (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧ 16*(C.gates.countP (fun g => g.inputs.length == 2)) ≤ 33*N
  let table := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (x y : I) =>
    C.eval (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach x y)
  ∃ Γ : Finset ℕ, Γ ⊆ Finset.range N ∧ Γ.card = Q ∧
    PEqualNP.Represents.HasLitSize (k+k) (PEqualNP.Represents.adjFun (k := k) (l := k) (target Γ))
      (150*(k+1)^2) ∧
    ∀ f g : I → Bool,
      let loss := fun (H : I → I → Bool) (D : Finset ℕ) =>
        (Finset.univ.filter (fun z : I × I => H z.1 z.2 ≠ xor (target D z.1 z.2) (xor (f z.1) (g z.2)))).card
      ∃ C₀, fits C₀ ∧ (∀ D : Finset ℕ, D ⊆ Γ → loss (table C₀) D = N*D.card) ∧
        ∀ t : ℕ, t ≤ Q →
          let sets := Γ.powersetCard t
          let opt := N * min t (Q-t)
          (∀ H : I → I → Bool, opt ≤ sets.sup (loss H)) ∧
          (∃ H : I → I → Bool, sets.sup (loss H) = opt) ∧
          ∀ (l : ℕ) (w : Fin l → ℝ) (C : Fin l → PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
            (∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) → (∑ i, w i) = 1 → (∀ i, fits (C i)) →
            ∃ D ∈ sets,
              let err := ∑ i : Fin l, w i * (loss (table (C i)) D : ℝ)
              (opt : ℝ) ≤ err ∧ (Q < 2*t →
                ((128*(N*(Q-t))+N*(2*t-Q) : ℕ) : ℝ) < 128*err)
changed.unlocks: Separates the unrestricted and randomized budgeted worst-case error above half of a structured shift support.
changed.context: Use the complete cubic graph. Its switched distance is at least 2(Q-2), with ≤Q edits per row. Apply the square-density gate bound at v=Q-10 to force full-support loss above NQ/128. For a uniform t-subset of Q shifts, mean loss is the mixture of empty- and full-support losses with weights 1-t/Q and t/Q. Those endpoint losses sum to at least NQ. Average over the circuit weights and select one subset meeting the mean. The bare and full tables attain the unrestricted optimum on their respective halves.

changed.title: Two biased outcomes attain optimal matching error exactly when the matching count is a sum of two divisors of the edit cap
changed.statement:
∀ (N q E t : ℕ), 0 < N → 0 < E → E ≤ N → E < q → q < 2*t → t < q →
  let X := Fin N
  let I := Fin q
  let Circ := PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit
  let legal := fun C : Circ =>
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (N+N) C ∧ C.output < N+N+C.size ∧
    ∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2 ∧
      (g.op = .and ∨ g.op = .or ∨ (g.op = .not ∧ g.inputs.length = 1))
  let table := fun (C : Circ) (x y : X) => C.eval (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach x y)
  ∀ (base : Circ), legal base → ∀ f : I → Equiv.Perm X,
    (∀ x : X, Function.Injective (fun j => f j x)) →
    let loss := fun (H : X → X → Bool) (D : Finset I) =>
      ((Finset.univ : Finset (X × X)).filter (fun z => H z.1 z.2 ≠
        xor (table base z.1 z.2) (decide (z.2 ∈ D.image (fun j => f j z.1))))).card
    let fits := fun C : Circ => legal C ∧ C.gates.take base.size = base.gates ∧
      C.size ≤ base.size+2*E+3 ∧ loss (table C) ∅ ≤ E
    let ideal := q*N*t-(2*t-q)*E
    (∀ (n : ℕ) (w : Fin n → ℝ) (H : Fin n → X → X → Bool),
      (∀ s, 0 ≤ w s) → (∑ s, w s) = 1 → (∀ s, loss (H s) ∅ ≤ E) →
      ∃ D : Finset I, D.card = t ∧ (ideal : ℝ) ≤
        (q : ℝ) * ∑ s : Fin n, w s * (loss (H s) D : ℝ)) ∧
    ((∃ (A B : Circ) (p : ℝ), fits A ∧ fits B ∧ 0 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 1 ∧
      ∀ D : Finset I, D.card = t →
        (q : ℝ)*(p*(loss (table A) D : ℝ)+(1-p)*(loss (table B) D : ℝ)) ≤ (ideal : ℝ)) ↔
      ∃ u v : ℕ, 0 < u ∧ 0 < v ∧ u+v = q ∧ u ∣ E ∧ v ∣ E) ∧
    ∀ m : ℕ, 0 < m →
      ((∃ C : Fin m → Circ, (∀ s, fits (C s)) ∧
        ∀ D : Finset I, D.card = t →
          q*(∑ s : Fin m, loss (table (C s)) D) ≤ m*ideal) ↔ q ∣ m*E)
changed.unlocks: Distinguishes the number of biased outcomes from the number of fixed-length fair bits at optimal matching error.
changed.context: Averaging a uniform t-set forces every used branch to spend E edits inside the matchings at equality. Swapping one index forces each expected matching count to equal E/q. This lies strictly between zero and one, so two branches have disjoint supports covering q indices. Each branch has a constant positive count on its support, whose size divides E. Conversely partition into divisor-sized blocks, put E divided by the block size on each index, and weight each block by its size over q. For m equal seeds, integer counts require q dividing mE. Cyclic allocation attains it.

changed.title: Pinning opposite controls in a binary read-once AND/OR tree isolates the partners of a distinguished input among its accepted pairs
changed.statement:
∀ (N : Nat) (F : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (x : Fin 4 ↪ Fin N),
  let tree := fun D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit =>
    (∀ g ∈ D.gates, (g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∨ g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or) ∧ g.inputs.length = 2) ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack N D ∧
    (D.output + 1 = N + D.size ∨ (D.size = 0 ∧ D.output < N)) ∧
    (∀ i < N, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.readsIn D (Finset.range D.size) i ≤ 1) ∧
    (∀ j < D.size, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.readsIn D (Finset.range D.size) (N+j) =
      if j+1 = D.size then 0 else 1)
  let val := fun (D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (s : Finset (Fin N)) =>
    D.eval (List.ofFn (fun z : Fin N => decide (z ∈ s)))
  let other := fun z : Fin N => ∀ i : Fin 4, z ≠ x i
  let keep := fun z : Fin N => z = x 3 ∨ other z
  let E := fun i j : Fin N => val F {x 1,i,j}
  tree F → val F ∅ = false → (∀ z, val F {z} = false) →
  val F {x 0,x 3} = true → val F {x 1,x 2} = true →
  val F {x 0,x 2} = false → val F {x 1,x 3} = false →
  (∀ z, other z → val F {x 0,z} = false ∧ val F {x 1,z} = false) →
  (∀ a b c d, keep a → keep b → keep c → keep d →
    E a b = true → E c b = true → E c d = true → E a d = true) ∧
  ∀ t i, keep t → keep i → i ≠ x 3 → E (x 3) t = true → E i t = false
changed.unlocks: Rules out a residual partner of the high control also serving another line, the case left by rectangle closure.
changed.context: Locate the AND gates of the two minimal true pairs. If they coincide, h and P enter one OR side, l and Q the other, so pinning l masks Q. If distinct, they feed separate OR branches. The high branch factors as (Q OR U) AND (h OR V) on disjoint subtrees, and U has no true singleton by the neutral-pair hypothesis. A partner t of Q must make V true alone. With i,t and Q off the high branch fails, and the other branches see at most i, which fails alone. Rectangle closure follows by simplifying the pinned tree.

changed.title: A partial matching behind the four distinguished one-hot lines has an explicit n+m-1 gate circuit with exactly one NOT
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : Nat) (A : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (x : Fin 4 ↪ Fin n) (y : Fin 4 ↪ Fin m),
  (
  let R := fun i : Fin n => i ≠ x 0 ∧ i ≠ x 1 ∧ i ≠ x 2
  let T := fun j : Fin m => j ≠ y 0 ∧ j ≠ y 1 ∧ j ≠ y 2
  (∀ j, A (x 0) j = decide (j = y 2) ∧ A (x 1) j = decide (j = y 3) ∧
    A (x 2) j = decide (j ≠ y 1)) ∧
  (∀ i, A i (y 0) = decide (i = x 2) ∧ A i (y 1) = decide (i = x 3) ∧
    A i (y 2) = decide (i ≠ x 1)) ∧ A (x 3) (y 3) = false ∧
  (∀ i j l, R i → T j → T l → A i j = true → A i l = true → j = l) ∧
  (∀ j i k, T j → R i → R k → A i j = true → A k j = true → i = k) ∧
  (∀ i, R i → i ≠ x 3 → ∃ j, T j ∧ A i j = true) ∧
  (∀ j, T j → j ≠ y 3 → ∃ i, R i ∧ A i j = true)) →
  ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n+m) C ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents A C ∧
    C.size = n+m-1 ∧ ∃! j : Fin C.gates.length, (C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not
changed.unlocks: Realizes every candidate residual matching within the same total gate budget.
changed.context: Let W,P,Q be the mixed row-column ORs at indices 1,2,3. Start with (P AND NOT W) OR (Q AND W). For a residual edge at row 3 or column 3, OR its other input into the positive W operand of the Q branch. This costs one gate per such edge. For every remaining matching edge OR in the AND of its inputs, costing two. The initial seven gates cover four lines per bank and the matching covers every additional line exactly once. The final size is seven plus the number of additional lines.

We hold a circuit of 10 AND/OR gates (three plain forms, full lines taken out, equal gates merged and unread gates dropped); at this size those forms are weak; we hold none of 9; this is a search. changed.title: Selected circuit gates can be copied in order with independently supplied boundary wires and the entire selected wire trace preserved
changed.statement:
∀ (N k s : Nat) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (J : Fin s ↪ Fin C.size)
    (port : Fin k ↪ Fin (N+C.size)) (o : Fin (N+C.size)),
  let old := List.ofFn (fun b : Fin k => (port b).val) ++
    List.ofFn (fun i : Fin s => N+(J i).val)
  StrictMono J → (∀ b i, (port b).val ≠ N+(J i).val) →
  (∀ i (w : Nat), w ∈ (PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C (J i).val).inputs →
    w < N+(J i).val ∧ ((∃ b, (port b).val = w) ∨ ∃ j, j < i ∧ N+(J j).val = w)) →
  o.val ∈ old →
  ∃ D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, D.size = s ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack k D ∧
    old.getD D.output (N+C.size) = o.val ∧
    (∀ i : Fin s,
      let d := PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt D i.val
      let g := PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C (J i).val
      d.op = g.op ∧ d.inputs.map (fun w => old.getD w (N+C.size)) = g.inputs) ∧
    ∀ v : Nat → Bool,
      (∀ i : Fin s, let g := PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C (J i).val
        v (N+(J i).val) = g.op.eval (g.inputs.map v)) →
      let z := List.ofFn (fun b : Fin k => v (port b).val)
      D.wires z = z ++ List.ofFn (fun i : Fin s => v (N+(J i).val)) ∧ D.eval z = v o.val
changed.unlocks: Copies the three gate regions with their ordered operands and all independently supplied port values.
changed.context: Assign local wire numbers first to the boundary list and then to selected gate outputs in their old order. This combined list is injective. Invert each original operand on its unique name and copy the gate operation. The boundary condition makes each operand earlier. Invert the chosen output too. Empty gate lists use the selected boundary output.
